_comment: EXP 56 ARM A -- ONE MODEL WITH AGENTS AND TOOLS. A single seat, CC2 (Opus via the claude CLI), which is the only seat in the roster with NATIVE shell tools rather than the execute_python function-call loop the OpenAI-compatible routes get. That is deliberate and it biases the comparison IN FAVOUR of this arm: the founder's question is whether a researcher with one model and a shell can do without a second vendor, so the single-model arm is given the strongest configuration available rather than a handicapped one. It also costs 0 paid dispatches, because CC2 bills against the Max subscription. Every key except `models` and `experiment_name` is byte-identical to the other two arms; that identity is asserted by bench/tests/test_d9_d11_configs_valid_2026-09-05.py rather than maintained by hand.
_stall_gamma_note: Stall-path gamma thresholds sit above the gamma ceiling (1.0) so the stall detector can never fire via gamma; convergence rests on the two-sided gamma-alt gate. Config-level guard, identical to Exp 42/53/55.
_merge_arbitration_note: OFF IN ALL THREE ARMS, AND THIS IS A DECLARED DELTA FROM EVERY CONFIG exp40-exp55, WHICH ALL SET IT TRUE. Two reasons, and the second is the binding one. (1) The merge path is dead code: when arbitration votes MERGE the runner records merge_blocked_reason, logs MERGE WITHHELD and returns KEEP_DISTINCT, closed deliberately by the no-voting ruling of 2026-08-19. So arbitration buys nothing and costs dispatches. (2) THE CONTEXT IT ARMS READS THE WRONG PANEL LIST. In run_experiment, `_merge_arb_ctx` is populated with `"panel": list(exp_config.models)` -- the orchestrator's full 5 ModelConfigs -- never intersected with cfg.models. Every experiment to date declared all 5, so the two lists agreed and the bug was latent. Arm A declares 1 seat, so an armed arbitration would dispatch the other 4 vendors INSIDE the single-model arm and silently convert it into a panel. Off in all three arms holds it constant and closes the leak.
_apply_fixes_back_note: Frozen target. The three arms must review the same bytes; a target that repairs itself between arms would make the later arm an easier exam. Target integrity is additionally hashed per round by the runner.
_sk_note: S_k ON in all three arms. TURNED ON 2026-09-10 17:58 BST on the founder's explicit instruction: "Just do it all (turning on the admissibility gate too, if its off)". THE EARLIER REASON FOR OFF IS SUPERSEDED, NOT DELETED, and it read: the admissibility gate has never rejected anything, 0 of 3816, Wilson [0.0000, 0.0010], and the repair-or-remove ruling was outstanding, so running a mechanism under adjudication inside a comparison experiment added a variable without adding information. WHAT CHANGED. The repair landed: the CORRECTED break-even now decides, per his ruling of 2026-09-06 that it is better to run with corrected values and precision. Measured over a 2475-point grid in sk, nu_b, nu_f, q and R, the corrected gate is STRICTER at 502 points, 20.2828%, Wilson [18.7453%, 21.9125%], and LOOSER at 0, Wilson [0.0000%, 0.1550%] -- it can only ever reject more, never admit more. Against 326 archived shadow records the corrected and shipped verdicts AGREE 326 of 326, so on real data it would have changed nothing. Enabling it therefore adds no admission risk to the comparison. IT IS NOT DEAD CODE. Before the 2026-08-01 hard-gate repair the pipeline REJECTED everything and halted visibly; that repair turned a loud failure into a silent one, which is why the post-repair archive shows 0 rejections. The founder's recollection and the earlier note describe different periods and both are correct. THE PROSE HAZARD IS HANDLED ELSEWHERE AND IS NOT A REASON TO KEEP THIS OFF. On a non-Python target S_k inverts -- ruff cannot parse the file, so a shell injection inside a fence scored 1.0000 ADMISSIBLE while a correct prose fix scored 0.6667. The runner now FORCES sk_enabled off for any target that is not a Python module. All three arms are target_kind python_module, so the gate runs where it is defined and is disabled where it is not, automatically. **CORRECTED 2026-09-10 18:05 BST, AND THE FOUNDER'S RECOLLECTION WAS RIGHT WHERE THIS NOTE WAS MISLEADING.** The claim that the gate "has never rejected anything" is true ONLY of the threshold SUB-GATE: `passes_threshold` reads false 0 of 4142 times, Wilson [0.0000%, 0.0927%]. **The S_k pipeline AS A WHOLE has rejected 520 of 5834 outcomes, 8.9133%**, Wilson [8.2089%, 9.6717%], Clopper-Pearson [8.1942%, 9.6737%] -- through the hard gates and the effect gates, which sit before the threshold. He said it had "triggered in at least some small percentage of cases"; 8.91% is that percentage, and this note read as though the whole gate were inert. **AND NO_SCORE HAS NEVER OCCURRED: 0 of 5834**, Wilson [0.0000%, 0.0658%] -- every archived run targeted Python, so the prose short-circuit has never fired in practice. **IT IS NOT A CONVERGENCE BLOCKER AND CANNOT BECOME ONE.** `apply_sk_to_rk` returns R_k UNCHANGED on NO_SCORE: "the fix was never assessed, so its efficacy enters as zero MOVEMENT, not as a zero SCORE". The alternative was measured and rejected: scoring it 0 maximises the re-injection term and would push R_k from 0.500 to 0.620 per unassessed prose finding, accruing fabricated risk no prose run could ever work off.
_falsifier_gate_note: ON IN ALL THREE ARMS AND IT IS THE PRIMARY METRIC'S SOURCE. The gate re-runs each critical's falsifier itself and that verdict, never the model's prose, decides CONFIRMED. It also hands execute_python to the OpenRouter and DeepSeek routes during review. Turning it off would leave the arms with no answer-key-free truth criterion, which is the whole reason this design needs no seeded catalogue.
_routing_note: ON IN ALL THREE ARMS since 2026-09-09, and the defect that justified holding them off is repaired rather than tolerated. WAS: `_apply_routing` built its ladder from `exp_config.models`, the orchestrator's full roster, never intersected with cfg.models, so Arm A (1 declared seat) would have dispatched to exactly the 4 vendors it exists to do without, 3 of them paid. NOW: both call sites take `_declared_models(exp_config, cfg)`, which intersects the roster with the arm's declaration and normalises the -SIM suffix. Executed against these 3 config files, not asserted: Arm A keeps ['CC2'], Arm C keeps ['Codex', 'ChatGPT'], the 5-seat arm keeps all 5. Pinned by test_declared_models_roster_2026-09-09.py. The stale hardcoded default of `RunnerConfig.models` is treated as no declaration at all, because reading it as one erased the roster whenever the 2 vocabularies were disjoint. Archive reach of that erasure, measured by scripts/roster_disjointness_2026-09-09.py: 0 of 60 runs, Wilson [0.0%, 6.0%] -- real and reachable, never suffered. CONSEQUENCE, PRE-REGISTERED AND UNCHANGED: in Arm A the ladder is EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION even with routing on, because `route` excludes the finding's own source model and Arm A has only that one seat -- `rank_falsifier_writers(['CC2'], exclude=('CC2',))` returns 0 rungs. So Arm A still has no absorber between the falsifier gate and the HIL queue, escalations still accumulate, and a halt on HALTED_IRREDUCIBLE_QUEUE_ALARM remains a reportable outcome of this design rather than a mechanical fault to be tuned away. That halt was UNREACHABLE until 2026-09-09: an empty ladder was classified as a dead transport and retried forever, so the finding entered no queue count and the alarm could not fire. It is now stamped `routing_deferred` with a reason, and counted. Pinned by test_empty_ladder_is_not_a_dead_transport_2026-09-09.py.
_sweep_note: ON IN ALL THREE ARMS since 2026-09-09, 2 rounds each, same repair as the routing note above. WAS: `_post_convergence_sweep` iterated `for mc in exp_config.models` with no cfg.models filter, so a sweep in Arm A would have dispatched all 5 seats after the verdict. NOW it iterates `_declared_models(exp_config, cfg)`. Demonstrated by execution with a stubbed dispatcher in test_declared_models_roster_2026-09-09.py, which asserts on the seats actually reached rather than on the source text of the loop.
_immune_memory_note: OFF IN ALL THREE ARMS. Immune memory persists findings ACROSS runs. With it on, whichever arm runs second inherits the first arm's findings and the comparison measures run order instead of panel composition. This is the one cross-arm contamination path the design can close outright, and it is closed.
_locationkey_note: Location keys are AST-symbol based and the target is a Python module, so the symbols exist. The location-keyed critical series is also what makes the primary metric a count of DISTINCT defects rather than of restatements.
_panel_cwd_note: UNSET, matching the runner's own documented convention: staged confinement is for exam runs, and a code run legitimately needs this repository so a falsifier can reach its target. Falsifiers are unaffected either way -- they execute in a throwaway temp cwd with the repo on PYTHONPATH. The cost of leaving it unset is recorded honestly in the design note as confound 6: the arm configs and the design note sit where a shell-bearing seat can read them.

_ouroboros._note: External literature retrieval OFF. A live retrieval would add an uncontrolled and arm-varying input to a comparison whose value rests on every input except panel composition being identical.

_arm.label: single_model_with_agents
_arm._paid_seats_note: CC2 dispatches through the claude CLI on the Max subscription and bills nothing per dispatch. This arm's paid-dispatch cost is 0, which makes any per-pound comparison against Arm B degenerate; cost is therefore reported in dispatches and wall clock, not currency.
_arm._single_seat_quorum_hazard: With 1 declared seat the external panel size is 0, so the severity-based confirmation quorum in `_update_finding_statuses` computes `required = min(2, 0) = 0` and `independent_count >= required` is satisfied with zero independent confirmations. Arm A can therefore write CORROBORATED against a finding nothing corroborated. This is NOT removable from a config. It is why the primary metric counts falsifier-gate CONFIRMED only, and why CORROBORATED is reported separately in every arm.

_convergence_criteria.description: TWO-SIDED GATE (founder ruling 2026-06-10; hardened_gate_enabled=false). gamma is ACTIVE and LOAD-BEARING. Converged iff ALL of: (1) gamma_critical >= 0.30 on the location-keyed critical series; AND (2) 3 consecutive rounds with zero NEW genuine critical (settled, verifier-filtered, location-keyed); AND (3) no unverified critical candidate pending (A4 fail-safe); AND (4) not contested, where un-demonstrated sub-criticals are a logged NON-GATING residual queue per FIX 1; AND (5) not churning; AND (6) irreducible queue within bound.
_convergence_criteria.pass_condition: gamma_critical >= 0.30 AND 3 consecutive zero-NEW-genuine-critical rounds AND no unverified critical pending AND not contested (FIX-1 semantics) AND not churning AND irreducible queue within bound.
_convergence_criteria.fail_condition: Any seat fails to produce parseable output in 2+ consecutive rounds; OR non-convergence, which is assumed MECHANICAL and diagnosed under cy -- do not demote gamma; OR HALTED_IRREDUCIBLE_QUEUE_ALARM, which in this design is a reportable outcome of running without a routing absorber.

_directives_live._section_10_note: Section 10 was established INERT on 2026-07-12 (A4): the flag never reaches RunnerConfig and no compelled-convergence text reaches dispatch. Recorded false for documentation accuracy.
_directives_live._section_18_asymmetry: Section 18 asks a seat to diverge from the other seats. With 1 declared seat there are no other seats, so the directive text is present and vacuous. Held ON in all three arms rather than off, because the mechanism under test IS having other seats: a multi-seat mechanism that degenerates gracefully in Arm A is part of the treatment, while one that silently re-dispatches the other vendors -- routing, sweep, merge arbitration -- is a leak and is switched off. That is the rule this config applies, and it is stated so the choice can be attacked.

_pre_registration: FROZEN 2026-09-05 BEFORE ANY DISPATCH. Exp 56 answers D9: does a panel of DIFFERENT models beat one model running with tools and agents? THE ARMS: A = 1 seat (CC2) with native shell tools; B = 5 seats, 4 vendors; C = 2 seats sharing weights, route and system prompt, differing only in composed phenotype (D11, the seat-contrast diversity arm). PRIMARY METRIC, answer-key-free: the count of DISTINCT criticals, keyed by code location, whose falsifier the runner independently re-ran and returned CONFIRMED. CORROBORATED is attestation rather than demonstration and is reported SEPARATELY, never added to the primary -- this matters most in Arm A, where the external panel size is 0 and the confirmation quorum `min(2, external_panel_size)` degenerates to 0. SECONDARY: rounds to terminal verdict, gamma_critical at verdict, HIL escalations, irreducible queue size, wall clock, paid dispatch count. WHAT REFUTES THE DIVERSITY CLAIM: B confirms no more distinct located defects than A, AND B's confirmed location set is a subset of A's -- the subset condition is the decisive one, because a higher count alone is not separable from run-to-run noise at n=1. A weaker economic refutation: B's confirmed defects per paid dispatch do not exceed A's, where A's paid dispatch count is 0. WHAT ARM C DECIDES: if C resembles B, the benefit tracks seat count and operating-condition variety rather than vendor diversity; if C resembles A, it tracks vendors. FAILURE MODES TO REPORT RATHER THAN TUNE: a halt on HALTED_IRREDUCIBLE_QUEUE_ALARM in any arm; a seat producing no parseable output; a non-convergence, which is assumed MECHANICAL and does NOT demote gamma. NO TUNING AFTER RESULTS. The one fallback permitted is declared here in advance and applies to ALL THREE ARMS IDENTICALLY OR NOT AT ALL: if every arm halts on the irreducible-queue alarm before earliest_stop_round, all three may be re-run once with max_irreducible_queue raised to 8, and both attempts reported.
_plan_ref: Founder verdict 2026-09-05, items D9 and D11: "Do it. Do both." Design note: experimental_notes/D9_D11_Experiment_Design_2026-09-05.md. Validation: bench/tests/test_d9_d11_configs_valid_2026-09-05.py.
_verification_note: CC2v VERIFICATION IS HELD CONSTANT AND IS NOT FILTERED, deliberately. `_verification_step` receives the unfiltered roster because it does not dispatch to it: it selects the single seat whose base label is CC2 as a verifier and skips if that seat is absent. A panel review on 2026-09-09 proposed filtering it for consistency with routing and the sweep; measured against these 3 files, that would keep CC2v in the 1-seat and 5-seat arms and remove it from the contrast arm (d11_seat_contrast_diversity_arm) alone, converting a constant into a confound in 1 of 3 arms. Refused. Pinned by test_cc2v_is_held_constant_across_arms_2026-09-09.py.
